findings: Resisted knee extension weak & painless (arthrogenic muscle inhibition from effusion, not a true contractile lesion)
Passive tibiofemoral AP glide (Lachman) positive — the definitive test
sttt.interpretation: Resisted knee extension is often weak/painless acutely, reflecting arthrogenic muscle inhibition from effusion rather than a true contractile lesion; the passive tibiofemoral AP glide (Lachman) is the definitive test.

cpa.pattern: "Inhibited, post knee injury/surgery" is the classic post-ACL finding; activate VMO before general quad strengthening. Fascial component (from source): Not applicable acutely; address quads inhibition.

kineticChain.name: Knee Valgus Stress Test

fields.label: Dynamic valgus on squat / single-leg squat / landing

kineticChain.chainEffect: Dynamic valgus on squat/single-leg squat/landing is explicitly documented as "the most common pattern in female ACL injuries"; driven by ankle DF + glute med, not the knee itself.

functionalScreen.name: Single Leg Hop Series
functionalScreen.note: The named return-to-sport functional screen for this exact injury (dynamic valgus + landing mechanics + ACL risk). FMA source note: Lachman/pivot reproduced in function; single-leg hop confidence.

findings: Resisted knee flexion may be relatively preserved
Passive posterior tibiofemoral glide (posterior drawer) positive — the definitive test, not a resisted-muscle one
sttt.interpretation: Resisted knee flexion strength may be relatively preserved; the passive posterior tibiofemoral glide (posterior drawer) is the definitive test for PCL injury, not a resisted-muscle one.

cpa.pattern: Popliteus can become "Overactive, posterior-lateral knee pain" secondary to PCL-deficient posterior laxity — screen once the acute phase allows. Fascial component (from source): Posterior capsule.

kineticChain.name: Tibial Rotation Assessment (Screw-Home Mechanism)
kineticChain.chainEffect: PCL laxity can disturb terminal-extension screw-home; check for an "absent screw-home" pattern.

functionalScreen.name: Double Leg Squat (general baseline)
functionalScreen.note: No PCL-specific named functional test exists in this app's library; rely on the joint-play STTT test above as primary. FMA source note: Posterior-drawer load reproduced in function; downhill/decline discomfort.

findings: Passive tibial rotation at 90° (McMurray-type) reproduces joint-line pain/click
sttt.interpretation: Strong resisted testing rules out a contractile source; the passive McMurray-type tibial rotation at 90° reproducing joint-line pain/click localizes the lesion to the meniscus.

muscles.name: Hamstrings (medial vs lateral per which meniscus)

cpa.pattern: Hamstrings may guard protectively depending on which meniscus is involved; not a primary compensation-pattern condition. Fascial component (from source): Joint-line capsular fascia.

kineticChain.name: Tibial Rotation Assessment
kineticChain.chainEffect: Passive IR/ER at 90° reproducing joint-line pain is the direct kinetic-chain correlate of a meniscal lesion.

functionalScreen.name: Double Leg Squat
functionalScreen.note: Deep flexion loading reproducing joint-line pain is the functional equivalent of McMurray-type provocation. FMA source note: McMurray/Thessaly & deep squat reproduce joint-line pain.

findings: Resisted tests around the knee usually painless (ligament, not contractile)
Passive valgus stress (medial gap) at 0°/30° positive — the definitive test
sttt.interpretation: Painless resisted testing rules out a contractile source; passive valgus stress (medial gap) at 0°/30° is the definitive test for MCL sprain.

cpa.pattern: Adductors ("Overactive, medial chain") and the pes anserine group often guard the medial pain secondarily. Fascial component (from source): Medial capsule / pes anserine fascia.

kineticChain.name: Knee Valgus Stress Test

fields.label: Manual valgus stress at 0°/30° (grading MCL laxity)

kineticChain.chainEffect: The direct match, including its manual valgus-stress component at 0°/30° used to grade MCL laxity.

functionalScreen.name: Forward Lunge
functionalScreen.note: Sagittal loading with a valgus-stress component if cutting/lateral movement provokes the medial pain. FMA source note: Valgus stress (0°/30°) & cutting reproduce medial pain.

findings: Resisted tests around the knee usually painless
Passive varus stress (lateral gap) at 0°/30° positive — the definitive test
sttt.interpretation: Painless resisted testing is expected; passive varus stress (lateral gap) at 0°/30° is the definitive test for LCL sprain.

cpa.pattern: TFL/ITB and Biceps Femoris (lateral chain) often become protectively overactive — check TFL "Overactive, IT band syndrome" pattern once acute phase allows. Fascial component (from source): Lateral capsule / ITB fascia.

kineticChain.reason: Knee Valgus Stress Test is valgus-focused; this app's KC library has no dedicated varus-stress equivalent — rely on the passive varus-stress STTT test above.

functionalScreen.name: Forward Lunge (general sagittal-plane screen)
functionalScreen.note: A general sagittal-plane screen; no LCL-specific named functional test exists in this app's library. FMA source note: Varus stress & lateral loading reproduce pain.

resisted.label: Resisted Knee Extension at 0–30° (VMO timing test)

findings: Resisted knee extension at 0–30° (VMO timing test) shows VL firing before/dominating VMO
Passive patellar glide shows a lateral bias / tight lateral retinaculum
sttt.interpretation: VL dominance over VMO on resisted testing plus a laterally-biased passive patellar glide is the classic PFPS maltracking pattern.

muscles.name: Glute Medius (hip)
muscles.state: Check — proximal weakness drives dynamic valgus

cpa.pattern: "Inhibited, VL dominant" is the textbook PFPS finding; also check Glute Medius (hip), since proximal weakness drives the dynamic valgus feeding PFPS. Fascial component (from source): Lateral retinaculum / ITB tightness.

kineticChain.name: Patellar Mobility Test
kineticChain.chainEffect: The direct match: "laterally biased, tight lateral retinaculum" is explicitly linked in the app's own data to "CPA: VMO inhibited → VL overactive."

functionalScreen.name: Wall-Slide PF-Compression Screen
functionalScreen.note: The named functional test for a PF pain arc. FMA source note: Single-leg decline squat & step-down reproduce anterior pain.

findings: Resisted knee extension strong but painful at the inferior-pole/patellar tendon — classic contractile-lesion pattern
sttt.interpretation: Strong-but-painful resisted knee extension localizing to the inferior pole is the classic Cyriax contractile-lesion pattern for patellar tendinopathy; a decline squat is the functional equivalent.

cpa.pattern: Overactive Rectus Femoris with VMO inhibition often accompanies jumper's knee; check VMO facilitation alongside tendon loading capacity. Fascial component (from source): Superficial front line (quad–patellar tendon).

kineticChain.name: Patellar Mobility Test (adjunct)

fields.label: Retinacular tension affecting tendon load line

kineticChain.chainEffect: Can be checked as an adjunct (retinacular tension affects tendon load line), but isn't primary here — the eccentric loading functional screen below is more direct.

functionalScreen.name: Eccentric Single-Leg Step-Down Screen
functionalScreen.note: The named functional test for reproducing tendon load pain. FMA source note: Decline single-leg squat loads and reproduces tendon pain.

findings: Resisted tests generally painless (non-contractile unless secondary tendinopathy)
Passive flexion/extension both restricted — capsular pattern (flexion >> extension)
sttt.interpretation: Painless resisted testing with a capsular-pattern restriction (flexion >> extension), leathery end-feel, and reduced patellar mobility with crepitus is the classic degenerative/osteoarthritic pattern.

muscles.name: Glute Medius (hip)
muscles.state: Often also inhibited, contributing to dynamic malalignment

cpa.pattern: VMO commonly inhibited with VL dominant, and Glute Medius (hip) often also inhibited contributing to dynamic malalignment — check both. Fascial component (from source): Global knee capsular fascia.

kineticChain.name: Patellar Mobility Test + Tibial Rotation Assessment
kineticChain.chainEffect: Crepitus with passive glide and restricted rotation both corroborate the capsular/degenerative picture.

functionalScreen.name: Double Leg Squat

fields.label: Pain onset angle and compensation strategy

functionalScreen.note: Bilateral loading to observe pain onset angle and compensation strategy (heel-rise, trunk lean). FMA source note: Capsular-pattern ROM loss; stairs & squat limited.

passive.label: Ober's Test (passive hip-adduction restriction)
options: Positive — reproduces lateral knee pain with Noble compression

findings: Resisted tests around the knee usually painless
Ober's test positive — key provocation reproducing lateral knee pain with Noble compression
sttt.interpretation: Painless resisted testing is expected; Ober's test (passive hip-adduction restriction) is the key provocation, reproducing lateral knee pain when combined with Noble compression.

cpa.pattern: "Overactive, IT band syndrome" is the textbook driver, always compensating for an inhibited Glute Medius; this exact pairing is documented in the app's own data. Fascial component (from source): Lateral line (ITB/TFL) tension.

kineticChain.name: Tibial Rotation Assessment

fields.label: Tibial IR restriction / lateral chain tightness
options: Restricted tibial IR — lateral chain tightness

kineticChain.chainEffect: Explicitly documented: "restricted tibial IR, lateral chain tightness... biceps femoris and IT band restricting IR."

functionalScreen.name: Eccentric Single-Leg Step-Down Screen

fields.label: Repetitive knee flexion-extension under eccentric load

functionalScreen.note: ITBFS is classically provoked by repetitive knee flexion-extension under eccentric load, which this test reproduces directly. FMA source note: Noble/Ober positive; single-leg squat shows valgus.
